canonical_examples.problem: Given that $P(A)=\dfrac12,$ $P(A \cap B)=\dfrac16,$ and $P(A \cup B)=\dfrac23,$ find $P(A'\cup B').$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\ \frac{2}{3} & =\frac{1}{2}+P(B)-\frac{1}{6} \\ P(B) & =\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{6}-\frac{1}{2} \\ P(B) & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we construct the corresponding Venn diagram and shade the region $A'\cup B'.$

$$
P(A'\cup B') = \dfrac1{3} + \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac56.

canonical_examples.problem: Given that $P(B)=0.6,$ $P(A\cap B)=0.4,$ and $P(A\cup B)=0.9,$ find $P(A').$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $P(A)$ using the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\ 0.9 & =P(A)+0.6-0.4 \\ P(A) & =0.9+0.4-0.6 \\ P(A) & =0.7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P({A}^{′}) & =1-P(A) \\  & =1-0.7 \\  & =0.3.\end{aligned}
$$
